REPORT DATE: 09-05-2021 REPORT TIME: 0500 UTC REGION: GULF OF MEXICO SUB REGION: N/A AREA/BLOCK: GRAND ISLE 19 IMAGE DATE: 09-04-2021 IMAGE TIME: 2353 UTC DATA SOURCE: COSMOSKYMED MODE: SCANSAR WIDE VV RESOLUTION: 30 METER LOCATION: 29°09"00" N/89°53"50" W AREA: 4.40 SQUARE KILOMETERS CONFIDENCE: HIGH REMARKS: POSSIBLE OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THIS ANOMALY IS UNCONFIRMED AS OIL. THE ANOMALY APPEARED TO EMANATE NORTHWESTWARD AND WESTWARD FROM AN OIL FACILITY, AND MEASURED APPROXIMATELY 11.0 NMI IN LENGTH AND UP TO 0.35 NMI IN WIDTH, WITH INCREASING WIDTH WITH DISTANCE FROM THE SUSPECTED SOURCE. THE ANOMALY APPEARED DARK AGAINST ITS BACKGROUND WITH SHARP EDGES, AND WAS MOSTLY DISTINCT FROM NEARBY FALSE POSITIVES. WINDS AT THE TIME OF THE IMAGE WERE AROUND 4 KTS FROM THE ESE. THE ANOMALY WAS CO-LOCATED WITH A PREVIOUS ANOMALY IN NRC REPORT #1315497. UNCERTAINTIES: THE WESTERN END OF THE ANOMALY BLENDED INTO NATURAL PHENOMENA, AS SO THE EXACT EXTENT OF THE ANOMALY WAS UNCERTAIN. HOWEVER, THE PREVIOUS REPORT FROM THIS LOCATION AND THE APPROXIMATE ALIGNMENT OF THE WIND DIRECTION WITH THE ANOMALY ALLOWED FOR HIGH CONFIDENCE.

///NOPAA-NESDIS REPORT.//// REMARKS: POSSIBLE OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THIS ANOMALY IS UNCONFIRMED AS OIL. THE ORIENTATION OF THE ANOMALY ALIGNED WELL WITH OCEAN CURRENTS DATA NEAR THE TIME OF THE IMAGE WHICH WERE MOVING TOWARDS THE NE AT 1.5 KTS. UNCERTAINTIES: THERE IS A PORTION OF POSSIBLE OIL NORTH OF THE ANOMALY. DUE TO NATURAL SEEPS, NEARBY OIL FACILITIES, AND THE PROXIMITY TO THE COAST, IT WAS UNSURE WHETHER IT WAS CONNECTED TO THE ANOMALY. ALSO, THERE WAS LITTLE TO NO WIND DATA AVAILABLE NEAR THE TIME OF THE IMAGE.

Report DescriptionPOSSIBLE, UNCONFIRMED OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. REPORT DATE: 04-14-2023 REPORT TIME: 0815 UTC REGION: GULF OF MEXICO SUB REGION: N/A AREA/BLOCK: SOUTH PASS SP0024 IMAGE DATE: 04-13-2023 IMAGE TIME: 2354 UTC DATA SOURCE: RADARSAT2 MODE: SCANSAR NARROW VV RESOLUTION: 50 METER LOCATION: 28°59"55" N/89°16"51" W AREA: 3.43 SQUARE KILOMETERS CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM-HIGH REMARKS: POSSIBLE, UNCONFIRMED OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THE SLICK WAS LINEAR IN SHAPE, HAD A DARK CONTRAST TO THE SURROUNDING ENVIRONMENT, POSSIBLY EMANATED FROM A WELLHEAD, AND WAS LIKELY ASSOCIATED WITH NRC# 1364073 (DATED 5-APRIL-2023). THE SLICK WAS APPROXIMATELY 8.31NM IN TOTAL LENGTH, AND APPROXIMATELY 0.39NM AT THE WIDEST POINT. WINDS NEAR THE TIME OF THE IMAGE WERE OUT OF THE SW BETWEEN 10-13KTS NEAR THE TIME OF THE IMAGE. SkyTruth Minimum Estimate: 0 gallons
Report Description
****WEB REPORT**** APPROXIMATELY 50 GALLONS OF NO. 2 FUEL OIL WAS RELEASED TO A STORM WATER CONVEYANCE SYSTEM WHEN A FITTING ON AN OIL CIRCULATING SYSTEM ASSOCIATED WITH THE BOILER SYSTEM AT CITY HALL, 95 PLEASANT STREET, GARDNER, MA FAILED. A TOTAL OF APPROXIMATELY 500 GALLONS WAS RELEASED IN THE INCIDENT, 450 GALLONS WAS RETAINED IN AN OIL-WATER SEPARATOR. THE BALANCE (APPROXIMATELY 50 GALLONS) WAS RELEASED TO THE STORMWATER CONVEYANCE SYSTEM WHICH EVENTUALLY DISCHARGES TO PARKER POND IN GARDNER, MA. RESPONSE ACTIONS INCLUDED REMOVAL OF OIL FROM THE OIL-WATER SEPARATOR, CATCH BASIN DECONTAMINATION AND PLACEMENT OF SORBENT BOOMS AT THE POINT OF DISCHARGE TO PARKER POND. THIS RELEASE WAS REPORTED TO MA DEP.

Report Description
34' LUHRS MOTORYACHT WAS TRANSPORTED TO LAKE VIEW MARINA AND LAUNCHED INTO EAGLE MOUNTAIN LAKE ON THE BOAT RAMP. BOAT TOOK ON WATER AND BECAME PARTIALLY SUBMERGED. UNLEADED FUEL WAS LEAKING FROM BOAT INTO RESERVOIR. SPILL WAS CONTAINED BY APPLYING ABSORBENT BOOMS AROUND BOAT AND CONTAMINATED WATER. A CONTAINMENT BOOM WAS PLACED AROUND THE OUTSIDE OF THE ABSORBANT BOOMS. TAS ENVIRONMENTAL APPLIED 10 BAGS OF CELL-U-SORB OIL ABSORBENT TO THE CONTAMINATED AREA. THE BOAT WAS REMOVED FROM THE WATER AND THE ABSORBENT WAS REMOVED AND PLACED IN SEALED DRUM FOR DISPOSAL. LAKE VIEW BOAT RAMP WAS CLOSED.
